story.value: Radium was discovered in 1898 by Marie Sklodowska Curie, a Polish chemist, and Pierre Curie, a French chemist.
Marie Curie obtained radium from pitchblende, a material that contains uranium.
Radium was isolated in 1911 by Madame Curie and Debierne.

uses.value: Radium is used to produce radon, a radioactive gas used to treat some types of cancer.
Radium was once used to make self-luminous paints for things such as watches and aircraft instrument dials.
A mixture of radium and beryllium gives off neutrons and is used as a neutron source.
